title: Thais Buy Twice Global Average of Health Food and Drink
paragraphs: The global health food market is growing, as consumers invest more in their well-being. In 2025, the health food market was valued at around $1 trillion — a figure that's expected to double by 2033.

Health-focused food and drinks are doing especially well in Thailand, where 80% of consumers report having bought them in the past 12 months. According to a report by PwC Thailand, this is more than double the global average of 35%.
And these aren't just food and drinks that are naturally healthy, like vegetables. Rather, these are specialty products that make specific claims about the health benefits of consuming them.
Seventy-one percent of Thai consumers also say they have bought vitamins, minerals or other dietary supplements in the past year, with 79% saying they take these regularly.

The PwC Thailand survey, which included 500 Thai consumers, also found that 68% expect to increase how many fruits and vegetables they eat, while 49% expect to increase their vitamin and supplement intake.
Thai people's interest in health doesn't end with diet either, with 33% saying they've bought exercise equipment over the last 12 months.
PwC Thailand said the findings show a significant change in Thai consumer behavior, as health becomes part of everyday choices and spending, not something people only prioritize when they're sick.
PwC also found that Thai consumers have a wide range of health goals, although there are some clear — if often overlapping — priorities.

Almost half say they want to live longer and have better overall health — but just as many say they want to reduce their stress and boost their mental well-being. And 45% also say they want to improve cognitive performance and concentration.

The survey also revealed consumers' food safety concerns. Nine in 10 say they're worried about chemicals and pesticide residues in food, while 87% are worried about ultra-processed foods, and 77% worry about microplastics.
PwC said this suggests that labeling products as "clean," "minimally processed" or "organic" is no longer just about marketing luxury, but is a driver of trust for Thai consumers.
